statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the 'giaddr' field in a DHCP message from a client is non-zero, the server sends any return messages to the 'DHCP server' port on the BOOTP relay agent whose address appears in 'giaddr'. If the 'giaddr' field is zero and the 'ciaddr' field is nonzero, then the server unicasts DHCPOFFER and DHCPACK messages to the address in 'ciaddr'. If 'giaddr' is zero and 'ciaddr' is zero, and the broadcast bit is set, then the server broadcasts DHCPOFFER and DHCPACK messages to 0xffffffff. If the broadcast bit is not set and 'giaddr' is zero and 'ciaddr' is zero, then the server unicasts DHCPOFFER and DHCPACK messages to the client's hardware address and 'yiaddr' address. In all cases, when 'giaddr' is zero, the server broadcasts any DHCPNAK messages to 0xffffffff.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When a server receives a DHCPDISCOVER message from a client, the server chooses a network address for the requesting client. Once the network address and lease have been determined, the server constructs a DHCPOFFER message with the offered configuration parameters and sends the DHCPOFFER message to the requesting client.
actions: insert xid from DHCPDISCOVER into DHCPOFFER xid field

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If no address is available, the server may choose to report the problem to the system administrator.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server SHOULD NOT reuse the selected network address before the client responds to the server's DHCPOFFER message. The server may choose to record the address as offered to the client.
actions: do not reuse selected network address until client responds
optionally record address as offered to client

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If an address is available, the new address SHOULD be chosen as follows:

statements.subject: server
statements.description: As described in section 4.2, a server MAY, for administrative reasons, assign an address other than the one requested, or may refuse to allocate an address to a particular client even though free addresses are available.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: While not required for correct operation of DHCP, the server SHOULD NOT reuse the selected network address before the client responds to the server's DHCPOFFER message.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The configuration parameters MUST be selected by applying the following rules in the order given below.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST return to the client:

statements.subject: server
statements.description: IF the server has been explicitly configured with a default value for the parameter, the server MUST include that value in an appropriate option in the 'option' field, ELSE

statements.subject: server
statements.description: IF the server recognizes the parameter as a parameter defined in the Host Requirements Document, the server MUST include the default value for that parameter as given in the Host Requirements Document in an appropriate option in the 'option' field, ELSE

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST NOT return a value for that parameter,

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST supply as many of the requested parameters as possible and MUST omit any parameters it cannot provide.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: the parameters MUST be identified by an exact match between the client's vendor class identifiers and the client's classes identified in the server,

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MAY choose to return the 'vendor class identifier' used to determine the parameters in the DHCPOFFER message to assist the client in selecting which DHCPOFFER to accept.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: DHCPREQUEST generated during SELECTING state: Client inserts the address of the selected server in 'server identifier'.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: DHCPREQUEST generated during INIT-REBOOT state: The client is seeking to verify a previously allocated, cached configuration.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: DHCPREQUEST generated during RENEWING state: the client is completely configured, and is trying to extend its lease. This message will be unicast.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: DHCPREQUEST generated during REBINDING state: the client is completely configured, and is trying to extend its lease. This message MUST be broadcast to the 0xffffffff IP broadcast address.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client receives no acceptable offers, the client may choose to try another DHCPDISCOVER message.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: DHCPREQUEST generated during REBINDING state: 'server identifier' MUST NOT be filled in, 'requested IP address' option MUST NOT be filled in, 'ciaddr' MUST be filled in with client's IP address. This message MUST be broadcast to the 0xffffffff IP broadcast address.
statements.post_cond: message.server_identifier = null & message.requested_ip_address = null & message.ciaddr = client.ip_address & message.destination = 0xffffffff
actions: set ciaddr to client IP address

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client SHOULD use the parameters in the DHCPACK message for configuration.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Client inserts the address of the selected server in 'server identifier', 'ciaddr' MUST be zero, 'requested IP address' MUST be filled in with the yiaddr value from the chosen DHCPOFFER.
actions: insert selected server address in 'server identifier'
fill 'requested IP address' with yiaddr from chosen DHCPOFFER

statements.subject: client
statements.description: 'server identifier' MUST NOT be filled in, 'requested IP address' option MUST be filled in with client's notion of its previously assigned address.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: 'ciaddr' MUST be zero.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Server SHOULD send a DHCPNAK message to the client if the 'requested IP address' is incorrect, or is on the wrong network.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the DHCP server detects that the client is on the wrong net (i.e., the result of applying the local subnet mask or remote subnet mask (if 'giaddr' is not zero) to 'requested IP address' option value doesn't match reality), then the server SHOULD send a DHCPNAK message to the client.
statements.trigger: wrong network detected for INIT-REBOOT client

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If not, then the server SHOULD send a DHCPNAK message to the client.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the DHCP server has no record of this client, then it MUST remain silent, and MAY output a warning to the network administrator.
statements.trigger: DHCPREQUEST received from INIT-REBOOT client with no server record
actions: remain silent (do not respond to DHCPREQUEST)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST set the broadcast bit in the DHCPNAK, so that the relay agent will broadcast the DHCPNAK to the client, because the client may not have a correct network address or subnet mask, and the client may not be answering ARP requests.
statements.trigger: sending DHCPNAK to INIT-REBOOT client via relay

statements.subject: client
statements.description: 'server identifier' MUST NOT be filled in, 'requested IP address' option MUST NOT be filled in, 'ciaddr' MUST be filled in with client's IP address.
actions: do not fill 'requested IP address' option

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client MAY choose to renew or extend its lease prior to T1.
statements.trigger: client chooses to renew lease before T1 expiry
actions: send DHCPREQUEST to renew or extend lease

statements.subject: client
statements.description: This message MUST be broadcast to the 0xffffffff IP broadcast address.
actions: broadcast DHCPREQUEST to 0xffffffff IP broadcast address

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The DHCP server SHOULD check 'ciaddr' for correctness before replying to the DHCPREQUEST.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A DHCP server MAY extend a client's lease only if it has local administrative authority to do so.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server receives a DHCPDECLINE message, the client has discovered through some other means that the suggested network address is already in use. The server MUST mark the network address as not available and SHOULD notify the local system administrator of a possible configuration problem.
actions: mark network address as not available
notify local system administrator of possible configuration problem

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST mark the network address as not available and SHOULD notify the local system administrator of a possible configuration problem.
actions: mark the network address as not available

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server marks the network address as not allocated upon receipt of a DHCPRELEASE message.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server SHOULD retain a record of the client's initialization parameters for possible reuse in response to subsequent requests from the client.
actions: retain record of client's initialization parameters for possible reuse in response to subsequent requests from the client

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server responds to a DHCPINFORM message by sending a DHCPACK message directly to the address given in the 'ciaddr' field of the DHCPINFORM message.
actions: MUST NOT send lease expiration time
include parameters as defined in section 4.3.1

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST NOT send a lease expiration time to the client and SHOULD NOT fill in 'yiaddr'.
actions: Omit lease expiration time from DHCPACK response

statements.description: INIT-REBOOT state: client sends broadcast DHCPREQUEST; server-ip MUST NOT be set; requested-ip MUST be set; ciaddr is zero

statements.description: SELECTING state: client sends broadcast DHCPREQUEST; server-ip MUST be set; requested-ip MUST be set; ciaddr is zero

statements.description: RENEWING state: client sends unicast DHCPREQUEST; server-ip MUST NOT be set; requested-ip MUST NOT be set; ciaddr is IP address

statements.subject: client
statements.description: REBINDING state: client sends broadcast DHCPREQUEST; server-ip MUST NOT be set; requested-ip MUST NOT be set; ciaddr is IP address

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From INIT-REBOOT, client sends DHCPREQUEST and transitions to REBOOTING (-/Send DHCPREQUEST)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From REBOOTING, receipt of DHCPNAK causes restart; client transitions to INIT (DHCPNAK/Restart)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From REBOOTING, receipt of DHCPACK causes client to record lease and set timers T1, T2, transitioning to BOUND (DHCPACK/Record lease, set timers T1, T2)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From INIT, client sends DHCPDISCOVER and transitions to SELECTING (-/Send DHCPDISCOVER)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In SELECTING, receipt of DHCPOFFER causes client to collect replies and remain in SELECTING (DHCPOFFER/Collect replies)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From SELECTING, client selects an offer and sends DHCPREQUEST, transitioning to REQUESTING (Select offer/send DHCPREQUEST)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In REQUESTING, receipt of DHCPOFFER is discarded; client remains in REQUESTING (DHCPOFFER/Discard)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From REQUESTING, receipt of DHCPNAK causes client to discard offer and transition to INIT (DHCPNAK/Discard offer)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From REQUESTING, if DHCPACK is not acceptable, client sends DHCPDECLINE and transitions to INIT (DHCPACK (not accept.)/Send DHCPDECLINE)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From REQUESTING, receipt of acceptable DHCPACK causes client to record lease and set timers T1, T2, transitioning to BOUND (DHCPACK/Record lease, set timers T1, T2)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In BOUND, receipt of DHCPOFFER, DHCPACK, or DHCPNAK is discarded; client remains in BOUND (DHCPOFFER, DHCPACK, DHCPNAK/Discard)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From BOUND, when timer T1 expires, client sends DHCPREQUEST to leasing server and transitions to RENEWING (T1 expires/Send DHCPREQUEST to leasing server)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From RENEWING, receipt of DHCPACK causes client to record lease and set timers T1, T2, transitioning to BOUND (DHCPACK/Record lease, set timers T1, T2)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From RENEWING, when timer T2 expires, client broadcasts DHCPREQUEST and transitions to REBINDING (T2 expires/Broadcast DHCPREQUEST)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From REBINDING, receipt of DHCPNAK causes client to halt network and transition to INIT (DHCPNAK/Halt network)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From REBINDING, receipt of DHCPACK causes client to record lease and set timers T1, T2, transitioning to BOUND (DHCPACK/Record lease, set timers T1,T2)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From REBINDING, receipt of DHCPNAK or lease expiry causes client to halt network and transition to INIT (DHCPNAK, Lease expired/Halt network)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The DHCPINFORM message is not shown in figure 5. A client simply sends the DHCPINFORM and waits for DHCPACK messages. Once the client has selected its parameters, it has completed the configuration process.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client begins in INIT state and forms a DHCPDISCOVER message.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Once the DHCPACK message from the server arrives, the client is initialized and moves to BOUND state.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: SELECTING state referenced in Table 5: 'Requested IP address MUST (in SELECTING or INIT-REBOOT)' and 'Server identifier MUST (after SELECTING)' in DHCPREQUEST.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: INIT-REBOOT state referenced in Table 5: 'Requested IP address MUST (in SELECTING or INIT-REBOOT)' and 'Server identifier MUST NOT (after INIT-REBOOT, BOUND, RENEWING or REBINDING)'.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: RENEWING state referenced in Table 5: 'Requested IP address MUST NOT (in BOUND or RENEWING)' and 'Server identifier MUST NOT (after INIT-REBOOT, BOUND, RENEWING or REBINDING)'.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: REBINDING state referenced in Table 5: 'ciaddr 0 or client's network address (BOUND/RENEW/REBIND)' and 'Server identifier MUST NOT (after INIT-REBOOT, BOUND, RENEWING or REBINDING)'.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client begins in INIT state and forms a DHCPDISCOVER message. The client generates and records a random transaction identifier and inserts that identifier into the 'xid' field. The client then broadcasts the DHCPDISCOVER on the local hardware broadcast address to the 0xffffffff IP broadcast address and 'DHCP server' UDP port.
statements.post_cond: client.xid_generated = true & client.local_time_recorded = true & client.dhcpdiscover_broadcast = true
actions: broadcast DHCPDISCOVER to 0xffffffff on DHCP server UDP port

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the parameters are acceptable, the client records the address of the server that supplied the parameters from the 'server identifier' field and sends that address in the 'server identifier' field of a DHCPREQUEST broadcast message.
statements.pre_cond: client.state = SELECTING & client.dhcpoffer_received = true & client.parameters_acceptable = true
actions: select one DHCPOFFER from collected offers
extract server identifier from DHCPOFFER server identifier option
broadcast DHCPREQUEST with server identifier and same xid as DHCPOFFER

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Once the DHCPACK message from the server arrives, the client is initialized and moves to BOUND state. The client records the lease expiration time as the sum of the time at which the original request was sent and the duration of the lease from the DHCPACK message.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Any arriving DHCPACK messages must be silently discarded (during DHCPOFFER collection phase, before DHCPREQUEST is sent).

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client SHOULD wait a random time between one and ten seconds to desynchronize the use of DHCP at startup.
actions: wait random time between 1 and 10 seconds before broadcasting DHCPDISCOVER

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MAY request specific parameters by including the 'parameter request list' option.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MAY suggest a network address and/or lease time by including the 'requested IP address' and 'IP address lease time' options.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MUST include its hardware address in the 'chaddr' field, if necessary for delivery of DHCP reply messages.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MAY include a different unique identifier in the 'client identifier' option, as discussed in section 4.2.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the 'xid' of an arriving DHCPOFFER message does not match the 'xid' of the most recent DHCPDISCOVER message, the DHCPOFFER message must be silently discarded.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Any arriving DHCPACK messages must be silently discarded.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client SHOULD perform a check on the suggested address to ensure that the address is not already in use.
actions: perform address-in-use check on suggested address (e.g., ARP probe)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When broadcasting an ARP request for the suggested address, the client must fill in its own hardware address as the sender's hardware address, and 0 as the sender's IP address, to avoid confusing ARP caches in other hosts on the same subnet.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the network address appears to be in use, the client MUST send a DHCPDECLINE message to the server.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client SHOULD broadcast an ARP reply to announce the client's new IP address and clear any outdated ARP cache entries in hosts on the client's subnet.
actions: broadcast ARP reply to announce new IP address and clear outdated ARP cache entries on subnet

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client begins in INIT-REBOOT state and sends a DHCPREQUEST message.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Once a DHCPACK message with an 'xid' field matching that in the client's DHCPREQUEST message arrives from any server, the client is initialized and moves to BOUND state.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client begins in INIT-REBOOT state and sends a DHCPREQUEST message broadcast on the local hardware broadcast address to the 'DHCP server' UDP port.
actions: insert known network address as 'requested IP address' option in DHCPREQUEST
generate and record random transaction identifier into 'xid' field
record local time for lease expiration computation
broadcast DHCPREQUEST to DHCP server UDP port on local hardware broadcast address

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Once a DHCPACK message with an 'xid' field matching that in the client's DHCPREQUEST message arrives from any server, the client is initialized and moves to BOUND state.
statements.pre_cond: client.state = INIT-REBOOT & message.type = DHCPACK & message.xid = client.xid
actions: record lease expiration time as sum of DHCPREQUEST send time and lease duration from DHCPACK

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MUST insert its known network address as a 'requested IP address' option in the DHCPREQUEST message.
actions: Insert client known network address as 'requested IP address' option in DHCPREQUEST message

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client may request specific configuration parameters by including the 'parameter request list' option.
actions: Optionally include 'parameter request list' option in DHCPREQUEST message

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MUST NOT include a 'server identifier' in the DHCPREQUEST message.
actions: Omit 'server identifier' option from DHCPREQUEST message

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Once a DHCPACK message with an 'xid' field matching that in the client's DHCPINFORM message arrives from any server, the client is initialized.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client sends a DHCPINFORM message. The client generates and records a random transaction identifier and inserts that identifier into the 'xid' field. The client places its own network address in the 'ciaddr' field.
statements.trigger: initialization with externally assigned network address
actions: generate and record random transaction identifier
insert transaction identifier into xid field
place own network address in ciaddr field
unicast DHCPINFORM to server if server address known, else broadcast to limited broadcast address

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Once a DHCPACK message with an 'xid' field matching that in the client's DHCPINFORM message arrives from any server, the client is initialized.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client SHOULD NOT request lease time parameters.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client does not receive a DHCPACK within a reasonable period of time (60 seconds or 4 tries if using timeout suggested in section 4.1), then it SHOULD display a message informing the user of the problem, and then SHOULD begin network processing using suitable defaults as per Appendix A.
actions: display message to user informing of the problem
begin network processing using suitable defaults per Appendix A

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When the DHCP client knows the address of a DHCP server, in either INIT or REBOOTING state, the client may use that address in the DHCPDISCOVER or DHCPREQUEST rather than the IP broadcast address.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client receives no response to DHCP messages sent to the IP address of a known DHCP server, the DHCP client reverts to using the IP broadcast address.
actions: revert to sending DHCP messages to IP broadcast address

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client unicasts DHCPRELEASE messages to the server. Because the client is declining the use of the IP address supplied by the server, the client broadcasts DHCPDECLINE messages.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Because the client is declining the use of the IP address supplied by the server, the client broadcasts DHCPDECLINE messages.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When the DHCP client knows the address of a DHCP server, in either INIT or REBOOTING state, the client may use that address in the DHCPDISCOVER or DHCPREQUEST rather than the IP broadcast address.
actions: use known server unicast address as destination instead of IP broadcast address in DHCPDISCOVER or DHCPREQUEST

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client may also use unicast to send DHCPINFORM messages to a known DHCP server.
actions: send DHCPINFORM via unicast to known DHCP server address

statements.subject: client
statements.description: T1 is the time at which the client enters the RENEWING state and attempts to contact the server that originally issued the client's network address.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: T2 is the time at which the client enters the REBINDING state and attempts to contact any server.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client has successfully reacquired its network address, returns to BOUND state and may continue network processing.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the lease expires before the client receives a DHCPACK, the client moves to INIT state, MUST immediately stop any other network processing and requests network initialization parameters as if the client were uninitialized.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: At time T1 the client moves to RENEWING state and sends (via unicast) a DHCPREQUEST message to the server to extend its lease.
actions: set ciaddr to current network address
record local time of DHCPREQUEST transmission

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When the client receives a DHCPACK from the server, the client computes the lease expiration time as the sum of the time at which the client sent the DHCPREQUEST message and the duration of the lease in the DHCPACK message. The client has successfully reacquired its network address, returns to BOUND state and may continue network processing.
actions: compute lease expiration time as DHCPREQUEST_send_time + lease_duration

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If no DHCPACK arrives before time T2, the client moves to REBINDING state and sends (via broadcast) a DHCPREQUEST message to extend its lease.
statements.pre_cond: client.state = RENEWING & timer.T2 = expired & DHCPACK.received = false
actions: set ciaddr to current network address

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In both RENEWING and REBINDING states, if the client receives no response to its DHCPREQUEST message, the client SHOULD wait one-half of the remaining lease time (in REBINDING state), down to a minimum of 60 seconds, before retransmitting the DHCPREQUEST message.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client MAY choose to renew or extend its lease prior to T1.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server SHOULD return T1 and T2, and their values SHOULD be adjusted from their original values to take account of the time remaining on the lease.
actions: include T1 option in DHCPACK adjusted for time remaining on lease
include T2 option in DHCPACK adjusted for time remaining on lease

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In both RENEWING and REBINDING states, if the client receives no response to its DHCPREQUEST message, the client SHOULD wait one-half of the remaining time until T2 (in RENEWING state) and one-half of the remaining lease time (in REBINDING state), down to a minimum of 60 seconds, before retransmitting the DHCPREQUEST message.
actions: if client.state = RENEWING: wait max(60s, 0.5 * (T2 - current_time)) before retransmitting DHCPREQUEST
if client.state = REBINDING: wait max(60s, 0.5 * remaining_lease_time) before retransmitting DHCPREQUEST

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the lease expires before the client receives a DHCPACK, the client moves to INIT state, MUST immediately stop any other network processing and requests network initialization parameters as if the client were uninitialized.
actions: immediately stop all other network processing
request network initialization parameters as if uninitialized

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client then receives a DHCPACK allocating that client its previous network address, the client SHOULD continue network processing.
actions: resume network processing with previously held network address

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client is given a new network address, it MUST NOT continue using the previous network address and SHOULD notify the local users of the problem.
actions: cease using previous network address immediately

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client no longer requires use of its assigned network address (e.g., the client is gracefully shut down), the client sends a DHCPRELEASE message to the server.
